sources.title: What does FATF travel rule mean for agent payments?
sources.body:
According to FATF, the FATF travel rule calls for relevant originator and beneficiary information to accompany covered virtual-asset transfers through regulated providers. [1]

FATF's virtual-asset guidance applies its risk-based framework to virtual asset service providers and explains implementation of the travel rule. These international standards are implemented through national law, so an application's actual duties depend on its jurisdiction, activity and counterparties. A public wallet address or transaction hash alone is not the complete customer-information exchange described by the framework. The 2021 guidance must be read alongside later FATF revisions. [1][2]

For an agent payment service, assess the parties, control over funds and actual service before drawing a legal conclusion about FATF travel rule. Testnet execution demonstrates a mechanism with faucet assets; it does not establish licensing, safeguarding or real-customer compliance. A small payment or an automated decision is not evidence of an exemption. The cited authority describes a framework, not a legal opinion about this product. [1]

Author interpretation: map the proposed business flow to the current rules with qualified local advice, preserve the basis for each conclusion and revisit it when the flow changes. Keep personal information out of public ledger memos and use appropriate private channels for necessary information exchange. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
